title: TCS Builds AI Platform to Accelerate Drug Discovery and Clinical Trials in India
excerpt: Tata Consultancy Services is developing an artificial intelligence platform aimed at speeding up drug discovery and streamlining clinical trial processes across the Indian pharmaceutical industry.
body:
• TCS is building a new AI-powered platform designed to accelerate drug discovery timelines and improve clinical trial efficiency in India.
  • The platform leverages machine learning and data analytics to identify drug candidates faster and optimize trial site selection.
  • India's pharmaceutical industry, which supplies over 50% of global vaccine demand and 20% of generic medicines, stands to benefit significantly from AI-driven drug development.
  • The initiative builds on TCS's existing Advanced Drug Development (ADD) suite, which already serves global life sciences clients.

Tata Consultancy Services is developing an artificial intelligence platform to accelerate drug discovery and clinical trial processes in India, the company announced. The initiative positions India's largest IT services firm at the intersection of two rapidly growing sectors: AI and pharmaceutical research.

The Platform

TCS's new platform applies machine learning algorithms and advanced data analytics across multiple stages of drug development — from initial target identification and compound screening to clinical trial design and patient recruitment. The system is designed to reduce the time and cost associated with bringing new drugs to market, a process that traditionally takes 10 to 15 years and costs upwards of $2.6 billion per approved drug globally.

The platform builds on TCS's existing Advanced Drug Development (ADD) suite, a cloud-based system that already offers services including clinical data management, metadata management, pharmacovigilance, and analytics. The ADD suite uses a cognitive engine called Decision Fabric that automates complex business processes in drug development.

"We are leveraging our deep knowledge of the life sciences industry to expand the capabilities of the TCS ADD suite of cloud platforms."

— Debashis Ghosh, President, Life Sciences and Healthcare, TCS

India's Pharma Opportunity

India's pharmaceutical industry is the world's third-largest by volume, supplying more than 50% of global vaccine demand and approximately 20% of the world's generic medicines. However, the country's drug discovery capabilities have historically lagged behind the United States and Europe, with most Indian pharmaceutical companies focused on generic manufacturing rather than novel drug development.

AI-driven platforms could help bridge this gap. Machine learning models can screen millions of molecular compounds in hours rather than months, predict drug-target interactions with increasing accuracy, and identify optimal patient populations for clinical trials. Several global pharmaceutical companies, including Pfizer, AstraZeneca, and Novartis, have already integrated AI into their drug discovery pipelines.

Competitive Positioning

TCS enters an increasingly competitive space. Bengaluru-based startups like Exscientia and Insilico Medicine have raised hundreds of millions of dollars for AI-driven drug discovery, while Infosys and Wipro have expanded their own life sciences practices. TCS's advantage lies in its established relationships with global pharmaceutical clients and its existing ADD platform infrastructure.

The company's life sciences and healthcare vertical has been one of its faster-growing segments, benefiting from increasing digitization across the pharmaceutical value chain. TCS reported consolidated revenue of approximately $29 billion in fiscal year 2026.

What's Next

TCS has not disclosed specific timelines for the platform's commercial launch or the scale of its investment. The company is expected to pilot the system with select pharmaceutical partners in India before expanding to global markets. The initiative aligns with the Indian government's broader push to position the country as a hub for pharmaceutical innovation, supported by regulatory reforms and increased R&D spending.
